title: Masking — local adjustments through gradients, brushes and non-AI range selections
objective: Deliver Lightroom-familiar local adjustments as a host concept over the delivered modules: a mask is an ordered list of combinable components in content coordinates, and every maskable module's existing controls apply through it. Linear gradients first, then radial gradients and combination, then brushes with feathering and erasing, then deterministic non-AI luminance and colour range selections. Several components of any kind combine in one mask by an explicit, reorderable list, which is the recorded UX improvement over Lightroom. Model-based selections, clone and heal stay out.
context_summary:
Masking is designed in docs/design/masking.md, authorized by the owner on 2026-09-23, and in progress on claude/masking-implementation-plan-b04e15. The coverage mathematics is frozen by docs/design/mask-study.md against the independent f64 reference at crates/lightwell-core/tests/reference/mask.rs; transcribe it, never re-derive it, and obey that study's Transcription section (no FMA, no reassociation, no precomputed reciprocals, no Horner-form smooth) — production code is bit-identical to that reference, not merely within a tolerance.

DELIVERED. Masks are host objects in the recipe beside the layers, so history, undo, preview, Restore and versions carry them with no new machinery. A layer carries an optional mask reference; one component-kind table holds the linear and radial gradients and drives parsing, the generated per-kind geometry methods and the generated controls alike, so registering a kind is what makes it creatable. The mask.* host command family is declared with the same ActionDescriptor, ParameterDescriptor and Control types a module uses, drafts through the delivered draft.* lifecycle, and labels entries by the design's granularity table. A maskable effect flag (Basic, the colour mixer, Presence) puts one optional host-owned mask field on every action of such a module, with per-target single_layer and placement after the global layer in mask order. The masked colour and masked spatial primitives blend the operation's output against its own input in linear light, so a masked layer changes a picture on the byte and RAW linear paths with render.sample equal to the rendered byte. A masked recipe is proxy eligible and its proxy frame equals the exact recipe over the exact downscale byte for byte; a feature thinner than two proxy pixels has its field supersampled on the proxy phase only. The mask overlay is a bounded display-cell coverage grid the exact preview phase returns beside its frame. render.transform answers the geometry tail as one affine so a gesture can map pointer positions without a round trip per move.

REMAINING. The Mask panel and canvas; phase A's rendered evidence; the component-list interface; phase B's evidence; brushes over the host path primitives and the content-addressed stroke store; non-AI luminance and colour range selections; and the full-editor acceptance pass.

CONTRACTS NOT TO BREAK. The catalog is format 6 and the recipe format 2: this branch and main each bumped to catalog 5 for a different shape (the mask table here, the preset library there), so the merged shape is neither and both earlier fives are refused by name. Geometry methods are generated per kind — mask.create-linear, mask.add-radial, mask.set-linear — and a mask, a component and a name travel in the request envelope rather than as declared parameters, because the closed parameter vocabulary has no string kind. An unknown component kind is treated exactly as an unavailable provider: retained everywhere, and refused for rendering, sampling, appending an edit and restoring. A masked layer must never be creatable before it is evaluable — the host compiles a recipe before persisting one, so a stage that cannot evaluate a mask refuses the commit rather than rendering as if unmasked.

HOW TO WORK ON THIS. Agent worktrees are routinely created from the wrong base — of six agents, one started on main, two on an unrelated branch and one on a diverged commit — so every agent must first check that a named delivered file exists and otherwise run `git checkout -B <task-branch> claude/masking-implementation-plan-b04e15`, which is never classified destructive. docs/features.md is the integrator's file: three merges in a row conflicted there because each agent described the whole feature from its own side. Timing figures are only quotable from a quiet host: record the one-minute load average beside every measurement and mark anything taken above about 8.0 provisional, because a masked-spatial run at load 87.9 measured identical unmasked work at 353 and 543 ms against a delivered quiesced 191 ms. api::owner::tests::racing_requests_supersede_the_pending_job_and_withdrawal_releases_only_its_own_interest is a known pre-existing flake under full-workspace load and is being fixed separately; it is not a masking regression.

tasks.description: Introduce the maskable effect flag, the host-owned mask target field on maskable actions, per-target single-layer semantics, and the placement and ordering rule for masked layers.
extra_context: This is the change that gives masking every delivered adjustment at once: Basic, the colour mixer and Presence declare maskable and nothing else does. No module code parses, plans or compiles the target; it is entirely host-owned.

single_layer becomes at most one layer of this effect per target, where the global layer and each mask are distinct targets. Two layers with the same target still fail with the existing ambiguous-layers validation error and nothing is rewritten.
Ordering is the part a person can see: masked layers of one effect follow the global one and are ordered by their mask's index, so overlapping masks apply in the order the mask list shows.

This task makes a masked layer creatable and the masked colour primitive task makes it evaluable. They must land in one integration, in that order, and never ship apart: between them a masked layer would render as if unmasked, which is exactly the silent omission the pillars forbid. The host compiles a stack before persisting it, so a temporary refusal in compile is not an option either — it would block the commit this task adds.

tasks.description: Build CompiledMask and the linear gradient component: stage-bound evaluation at pixel centres, a conservative bounds rectangle, the minimum feature size, and compilation with no pixel access.
extra_context: CompiledMask is the host's answer to what is this pixel's coverage, and it must answer for one pixel in bounded time so that render.sample can equal the rendered byte. No full-resolution mask plane is allocated anywhere, ever.
The bounds rectangle is what makes a small mask cheap on a 60 MP frame: outside it coverage is exactly zero, so a colour run skips those spans and a spatial tiling copies those tiles.

The production evaluation is the study's frozen equation transcribed in the same written form and the same order as the reference, as the vignette unit is, so the two are bit-identical rather than merely close.

Stored positions are normalized fractions in [-1, 2], not [0, 1]: the frame is [0, 1] and one stage extent of overshoot per side is legal, because a gradient dragged from off the canvas and a radial centred outside the frame are ordinary edits. Decided 2026-09-23 on the mask study's recommendation; every frozen equation is total on finite inputs, so this is a validation rule only.
The study froze the legal distance range at 1e-4 to 64 mask-space units, and the zero-length-axis rejection is the l2 >= 1e-8 form rather than a sqrt. Transcribe those, do not re-derive them.

tasks.description: Keep a masked recipe proxy eligible, and handle features thinner than a proxy pixel explicitly rather than silently.

tasks.description: Build the Mask canvas mode, the Masks panel and the linear gradient handle editor in the desktop, with the adjustments of the maskable modules bound to the selected mask.
extra_context: The desktop layering rules are enforced by the repository check, not by review: no Iced under state/, no core under view/, no core in the widget crate. The Masks panel is a view model plus a view, and the mask handle editor is a draft state machine beside the delivered crop one.

The adjustments inside a mask are not new controls. They are the delivered generated sections of Basic, Presence and the colour mixer, bound to the mask target, with the same widgets, the same draft lifecycle and the same Copy as JSON request, which now carries the mask.
Every handle has a number field, because no gesture may be reachable only by pointer.

A draft carries a mask target for a mask command but not for a module action, so a masked slider gesture commits through the action and does not preview. Adding the target to a module-action draft is this task's, and it is what makes a masked slider follow the drag the way a global one does.

Bind the existing generated sections to a mask rather than writing new controls. The tools panel derives its sections from Inputs.recipe (a RecipeDescription), and every layer row now carries its mask, so seeding a section from the masked layer is a matter of filtering by that field and parameterizing the derivation by target. The control's submitted request then carries the host-owned mask envelope field. This is the single biggest saving available in this task; do not reimplement Basic, Presence or the mixer inside a mask.

The command names are generated per kind: mask.create-linear, mask.add-radial, mask.set-linear and so on, with the kind in the method rather than a field. Component display names come from the host (Linear 1, Radial 2) and their ordinals are never reused.

Handles are drawn by mapping content coordinates through render.transform's affine to the output stage and then through the canvas View (scale and origin) exactly as crop_canvas.rs does. Unlike the crop draft, a mask draft shows the whole current render rather than a truncated prefix, because a mask does not change the stage. Do not call render.locate per pointer move.

crop_draft.rs and crop_canvas.rs are the delivered model for a canvas-takeover draft, its hit testing and its Apply/Cancel; follow their shape. The repository check enforces the layering rules: no Iced under state/, no core under view/, no core in the widget crate.

A draft carries a mask target for a mask command but not for a module action, so a masked slider gesture currently commits through the action and does not preview. Adding that target is this task's, and it is what makes a masked slider follow the drag the way a global one does. The core already holds Draft.target; the module-action path is what is missing.

The panel must surface the refusals the command family already makes rather than offering buttons that would be refused: a mask's only component cannot be deleted (offer Delete mask instead), a first component must be add, and an edit that would leave a non-add component leading is refused.
The overlay tint is green or white, never red: the delivered clipping indicators own red, blue and the magenta between them. The tokens are in crates/lightwell-ui/src/theme.rs.

tasks.description: Deliver the combination vocabulary: add, subtract and intersect modes across component kinds, per-component and per-mask inversion, mask amount, and mask reorder, duplicate and delete with their layer consequences.
extra_context: First, a correction found on integration: the command family declares its own geometry table (GEOMETRY in the mask command module) separate from the host's component-kind table, and forces every field through a normalized-position descriptor. The radial gradient is therefore evaluable but not creatable — mask.create still advertises only linear and only x0/y0/x1/y1, and a radius, an angle and a feather do not take a position's range. Two tables describing one thing is the defect; fix it before adding anything.

The decided shape: each kind declares its own ParameterDescriptors once, in its own module beside its payload parser, and the commands generate their geometry methods per kind — mask.create-<kind>, mask.add-<kind>, mask.set-<kind> — exactly as edit.<action> and query.<id> are already generated. A kind then becomes creatable by being registered. The kind-independent commands (delete, rename, duplicate, set-amount, set-invert, reorder, set-component-mode, set-component-invert, delete-component, reorder-component, list) keep their current shape and names.

This is the phase-B heart and the answer to the owner's complaint about Lightroom: a component's mode, inversion and position are properties you can change afterwards, not a consequence of which button created it.
The first component of a mask is always add; adding a subtract or intersect component to an empty mask is refused with its reason rather than silently creating an empty selection.
Reordering masks re-sorts the masked layers by the ordering rule in one transaction and moves nothing else.

mask.duplicate is delivered copying the mask and its components only, because the mask target on module actions did not exist when it was written and fabricating masked layers against an unseen rule would have been a guess. Completing it here is required: a duplicate must copy the layers bound to the mask as well, since a mask without its adjustments is not a useful copy, and the per-target single-layer rule is what makes the copy legal.

A re-sort of masked layers by mask order already exists as resort_masked_layers in the mask command module, written before the placement rule landed. Reconcile the two into one rule with one call site rather than leaving both; the placement rule is the authority.

tasks.description: Add the host path primitives and their storage: the points parameter kind with its decimation contract, and the content-addressed stroke store in catalog format 6, so no catalog ever holds embedded stroke points.
extra_context: Exactly one new parameter kind is needed for brushes, and it is a parameter kind rather than a control kind: the brush is a canvas interaction and no panel widget edits a path.

These are host primitives, not mask-private ones. The points kind, the stroke list semantics and the brush-paint canvas interaction are shared with the corrections design (docs/design/corrections.md, an unmerged owner-review proposal for Clone, Heal and AI Remove), which asks for the same brush under the name brush-mask. Name and place them so that design declares them for its own actions rather than adding a second brush system.

The store exists because every history entry stores a complete recipe, not a delta, so embedding a component's stroke list copies every earlier stroke in that mask and storage grows with the square of the stroke count: about 37.5 MB across history for 200 strokes of 100 points, against 364 KiB of distinct stroke data. The owner decided the content-addressed store on 2026-09-23; see the design's stroke-storage section for the figures and for why pure deltas were rejected.

The store shrinks the quadratic constant by about 53 times, from roughly 1.8 KiB to 35 bytes per stroke per entry. It does not make storage linear and no claim that it does may be written anywhere. The hash-chain variant that would be linear is recorded in the design and is not built.
Decimation happens on the desktop before a stroke is ever sent, to a stated tolerance; coordinates are stored at the precision a 16384 px side can resolve and no more.

tasks.description: Build the brush component on the host stroke primitives: ordered strokes referenced from the content-addressed store, each with its own size, feather, flow and erase flag, the capsule coverage field, the grid index over segments, and the accumulation rules.

Maximum along a stroke and screen union across strokes is the frozen rule and the reason is worth keeping in the code: one pass of the brush has one density whatever the pointer's sampling rate, while a second pass is a second object and does build up.

Density is not delivered; its Lightroom meaning depends on a build-up model along a single stroke that would make coverage depend on stamp spacing and therefore on resolution. Say so in the user guide rather than shipping a control that means something else.

The grid index is what keeps a point query bounded: a pixel tests only the segments in the neighbouring cells, and the declared occupancy cap is checked when the mask compiles, before a pixel is read.

Strokes are objects inside the component, not history events. Add strokes combine by screen union and are therefore commutative, so removing one is well defined; an erase stroke does not commute with an add, which is why the component stores its strokes in order and the component list shows that order.

The component references strokes in the host store rather than embedding their points, so this task never writes a payload holding coordinates. If you find yourself embedding points in a component payload, the store task did not land and you should stop.

Pointer positions map through the affine from render.transform, locally, with no hop per move.

tasks.description: Deliver the luminance-range and colour-range components, reading the input pixel of the operation they modulate, with their panel controls and their sampling gesture.
extra_context: An image-dependent component costs nothing during a render because the value is in the row being processed, and costs one delivered O(layers) sample at a point query. It must not become a second rasterization path.
The colour range samples colours from the photograph through the delivered pick machinery rather than inventing a second picking mode.
These components combine with gradients and brushes through the same frozen algebra, which is what makes a sky selection practical.

The mathematics is frozen in docs/design/range-study.md with its f64 reference at crates/lightwell-core/tests/reference/range.rs. Transcribe it; do not re-derive it, and obey the mask study's Transcription section (bit-identical: no FMA, no reassociation, no precomputed reciprocals, no Horner-form rewrites). The frozen tolerance is on the metric, at 1e-6 + 1e-6 times the reference magnitude.

The study escalated four proposals, P12 to P15, with recommendations rather than decisions. Settle P12 before writing the component; P13's bounds answer (whole stage, INFINITY, proxy frame not marked approximate) follows from it.

A range selection reads the operation's input pixel, so a layer ahead of it changes what it selects: the study measures a +0.75 EV layer taking a sky from fully selected to not selected at all. That is the honest behaviour, and the user guide has to say it rather than the component hiding it.

acceptance_criteria: An acceptance journey exercises every mask kind, every mode, inversion, amount, reorder, duplicate and delete, with masked Basic, Presence and mixer layers, through the panel and through an independent JSON client, and compares complete stacks, history, pixels and errors.
Live agents, draft conflicts, Discard and Reapply, historical preview, Restore, undo, redo and reopen all behave as the delivered contracts state, with masks present.
A missing original, a changed original and a disabled maskable module each report explicitly with masks in the recipe and discard nothing.
The source file hashes are unchanged across the whole journey.
Every measurement the feature claims is recorded in the performance plan with its scope, and every miss is stated with its figures.

docs/features.md, docs/plan.md, docs/user-guide.md and the design's status line describe the delivered feature and its explicit gaps, and this plan is deleted rather than archived once its outcome lives in those documents.
